svg.title: This identity retains the moving determinant and covariance; replacing either by its value at zero would lose the derivative argument. Here is a uniform estimate for the mass in (GL4). If a centered Gaussian covariance Q satisfies Q ≤cI, its one-coordinate exponential moment gives P(|Zi| ≥v) ≤2e−sv+cs2/2 for s ≥0: apply Markov’s inequality to e±sZi and add. If the number of coordinates is at most P ≥1, and Pv ≤D, the complement of the radius-D ball is contained in the union of those coordinate events. Indeed, if every |Zi| < v, then ∥Z∥≤ √ Pv ≤Pv ≤D. Thus its probability is at most 2Pe−sv+cs2/2.
